sections.title: Build clear past questions
sections.content:
For most past questions, use question word + did + subject + base verb: Where did you go? Why did she leave? Do not use the past form after did: say “did you go”, not “did you went”.

Türkçe ipucu: did’den sonra fiilin yalın hâli gelir. who is different when who is the subject: “Who called you?” has no did.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question.
Which question asks about an exact clock time?
choices: What time did the class start?

questions.prompt: Complete the question: “Where ___ you meet your friend?”
Which answer fits “Who called you?”
Choose the natural question about a reason.

sections.title: When or what time?
sections.content:
Use when for a general time or date: When did you arrive? — On Tuesday. Use what time for an exact hour: What time did you arrive? — At 7:30.

Notice the answer clues: on Monday, last week, in July usually answer when; at 6:15, at noon, at half past eight usually answer what time.

questions.prompt: Choose the best question for “At 7:30.”
choices: What time did the shop open?

questions.prompt: Choose the best question for “Last Friday.”

sections.title: Choose the right question word
sections.content: Use who for a person, where for a place, why for a reason, which for a choice from a limited group, and what for information in general. Say the question word first, then build the rest of the question carefully.

questions.prompt: ___ did you travel with? — My sister.
___ did you meet after class? — At the library.
___ did he leave early? — Because he felt ill.
___ bus did you take, the 12 or the 15?

sections.title: Read an interview
sections.content:
Read: “On Saturday, Deniz visited a small art market with a friend. They arrived at eleven o’clock and looked at paintings, jewellery, and handmade notebooks. Deniz bought a blue notebook because it was simple and useful. Later, they drank coffee near the river. They went home at four, tired but happy.”

Read once for the whole story. Read again and find the exact detail that answers each question.

questions.prompt: When did Deniz visit the market?
What time did Deniz arrive?
Why did Deniz buy the notebook?
Where did they drink coffee?

sections.title: Listen, pause, answer
sections.content:
Use a device read-aloud tool or ask someone to read this twice: “Ece missed the first bus because she left home late. She waited fifteen minutes, then she took the next bus. She arrived at work at nine twenty and apologised to her manager.”

First listen for the problem. Then listen again for the time and the solution. Repeat the three Past Simple verbs: missed, waited, took.

questions.prompt: Why did Ece miss the first bus?
How long did Ece wait?
What time did Ece arrive at work?

sections.title: Mini interview
sections.content:
Ask and answer these aloud: “What did you do yesterday?” “When did you start?” “What time did you finish?” Then add one follow-up question with who, where, or why.

For a fuller answer, use this pattern: “I ___ yesterday. I started at ___. I was with ___. I chose it because ___.” Ask your own follow-up question before you move on.

sections.title: Question-maker challenge
sections.content: Turn each answer idea into a complete past question. Then make a four-question interview about someone’s last weekend. Include one question with when, one with what time, one with who or where, and one with why.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct order.
Complete: “What time ___ the meeting finish?”
Which question asks about a person?
Choose the best answer to “When did you call her?”
Which question is a subject question?
choices: Who did you send the message to?
Who were you send the message to?
